label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Kristen,

It was my popcorn. Saturday, November 7, about 10:40, I put a bag in the break room microwave, hit the popcorn button and went out front. A customer needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and finding it took longer than I expected, maybe six or seven minutes. I left the microwave unattended. That was my mistake, not anything wrong with the microwave.

The popcorn burned, the alarm went off and we had to clear the store for about 25 minutes. The engine from up on Hertel responded. There was no damage, just smoke and a stink, but that doesn’t excuse having customers and staff standing outside in 30-degree weather.

I’m sorry I put everybody through that. The Hendersons are regulars and I expect they’ll be back, but I shouldn’t have given them a reason to leave a full cart behind. Denise is getting her coffee, too.

For the record, the September alarm wasn’t mine. That was the sensor in the paint aisle. I’m not trying to dodge Saturday, just want Gary’s file to have that straight.

One of the guys on the engine was Mikey Szymanski, who I broke in as a probie back in 2003. Thirty-one years on the job, and my first alarm as a civilian is over a bag of butter popcorn. Mikey will make sure I remember it.

I’ll cover the $175. You can take it out of my check or I can bring cash, whichever you prefer. I understand the popcorn rule and won’t do this again.

I’d really like to keep my Saturday shifts. I like the weekend crowd, and I need the hours for heating oil. I know you and Gary have to take this seriously. I’m asking you to let me keep working Saturdays and earn back your confidence.

Walt
